title: Bridging the Spatial Blind Spot in Pathology Foundation Models for Tumor Localization
abstract: Pathology foundation models (FMs) produce versatile patch-level features but discard inter-patch spatial context, leaving them ill-suited for dense prediction tasks such as tumor localization. Multiple instance learning (MIL) methods offer attention heatmaps as a localization byproduct, yet these maps are optimized for classification and exhibit poor spatial coherence. We present TGSR (Text-Guided Spatial Reasoning), a lightweight cross-modal framework that restores spatial context on pre-extracted features and grounds its predictions in language. TGSR comprises three components: (1) a one-hop spatial aggregation module that reintroduces neighborhood context, (2) a scale-aware router that dynamically balances macro- and micro-level analysis based on local tissue statistics, and (3) an uncertainty-aware two-stage training strategy that mitigates label noise from both ground-truth annotations and MIL-derived pseudo-labels. Classification is performed by cosine similarity against class prototypes derived from LLM-generated morphological descriptions, which makes the semantic target of the model editable at test time. With 527K trainable parameters on 512-dimensional features and no backbone modification, TGSR improves patch-level tumor localization on four datasets spanning three organs, raising Dice by up to 22% over probing baselines under supervised settings and by up to 80% relative over raw MIL attention under weakly supervised settings. Because the semantic target of the model is carried by the text prototypes, a model fitted on lymph node tissue can be applied to colon tissue by replacing the class descriptions, where it exceeds a linear probe trained directly on colon.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Personalization with Foundation Models for Wearable Stress Detection
abstract: Personalization in wearable-based stress detection remains challenging due to substantial inter-individual variability in physiological and behavioral responses. While traditional approaches rely on user-specific fine-tuning or costly self-supervised pre-training on large datasets, we propose a lightweight alternative based on retrieval-augmented personalization. Our method leverages frozen, out-of-domain foundation models to retrieve similar patterns from a target user’s history and encode them into a compact personalized embedding that modulates representations extracted by a lightweight transformer network. We evaluate our approach on the WESAD stress detection dataset with N=15 users, comprising wrist-worn physiological (EDA, BVP, temperature) and activity (accelerometer) signals, and report gains of +3.92% in accuracy and +4.76% in macro F1-score over a non-personalized transformer baseline, approaching supervised fine-tuning performance without requiring any labeled user data. We further show that temporal retrieval, where only prior user samples are available, achieves performance close to full intra-user retrieval, demonstrating robustness to limited user history. To further test personalization under these constraints, we conduct a cross-dataset experiment using K-EmoCon as the retrieval database, simulating a cold-start scenario with no in-domain data available for retrieval. We report no significant gains in this setting, confirming that our method genuinely benefits from intra-user retrieval rather than the retrieved context alone.

title: The CO2ST of Agentic AI in Research
abstract: Generative AI has been rapidly adopted into multiple research practices. In this paper, we focus on the newest trend, so-called agentic AI. We calculate the carbon footprint of using agentic AI in a simulation of an academic literature review. We show that the energy consumption increases proportionately with the level of agency, resulting in a carbon footprint about three times larger when moving from low agency to a multi-agent process. The most co2stly step of this system is processing large quantities of text by the LLM, and resource consumption grows proportionally to the model size. Finally, we show the energy consumption of the CPU and GPU during processing and illustrate that the use of LLMs versus other software largely drives the power consumption difference. We demonstrate that researchers may make environmentally sustainable choices in research practices by making deliberate choices about agentic AI use.1
journal: Adjunct Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Oracular Interfaces: Divination and Magic as material for probing interactions with AI
abstract: AI systems already sort, summarise, guide, approve, deny, and route people across institutions and services. House of IFs pushes that logic into a more explicit and absurd form to challenge whether they deserve the authority often granted to them. The project is an interactive installation centred on a web-based interface that generates a growing archive of AI-written omens from contemporary news. An agentic system (the "House") builds and maintains this archive of speculation, connects it to a shared memory system, and lets users query it through chat. By drawing on the protasis/apodosis (IF/THEN) structure of Mesopotamian omen tablets, the project parallels the correlative logic of large language models with a structured system of divinatory knowledge. The omens relied on the observation of terrestrial phenomena, which were interpreted as signs from non-human intelligences announcing future events. This textual corpus of knowledge contained the omens as well as interpretations and counter-omen (apotropaic) spells. The spells suggest a degree of agency in responding to the events. By "Oracular Interfaces", I mean interactive works which call into question the discursive authority of AI systems, drawing on the Latin etymology of orare: to speak or pray. The oracle can be both the future-oriented pronouncement and its source: the role of the oracle may fall either on the interface or on the one wielding it. Here, “oracular” is used to describe the assemblage of the LLM and its surrounding system. The interface is the seam through which the elements that perform textual knowledge are surfaced for interpretation and questioning. The work situates itself within a growing body of academic writing that uses magic as a framing for AI and computation. This project contributes by drawing specifically and metaphorically on divination as a historically situated, structured interpretive practice, with formal procedures and socially mediated acts of reading. The metaphor enables the work's contribution: to make strange the now too familiar epistemic presence of AI systems. House of IFs is presented through a web interface showing individual omens (Figure 1), a chronological archive (Figure 2), rearrangeable tablets and interpretation tools (Figure 3), and a semantic map of the archive (Figure 4). An e-ink artefact serves as a tangible controller (Figure 5). An agentic system crawls, connects, and interprets contemporary news into divinatory texts. Unusual events, or faits divers, are placed in relation to major headlines through correlative association (a 2:2 pair of matching sign and signified). The interface slows the reading of the omen by splitting the structure across “tablets” which hold the IF/THEN structure, the interpretation (exegesis), the sources and the counter-spell. Some tablets are initially concealed and are revealed when participants hover over them. At NordiCHI, participants will use the web interface and e-ink controller to browse, reveal, rearrange and interpret omens as a shared, tangible encounter. Participants may also propose omens based on their lived experiences. This aims to be a collective platform to question the role of knowledge systems in shaping and mediating our connection to events in the world. House of IFs uses the omen form and the semiotics of the interface to invite reflection on how AI systems fabricate authority and meaning, to challenge how these systems become persuasive and ubiquitous across the mundane and consequential.
journal: Adjunct Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Human–AI Agent Collaboration for Industrial Problem Solving: A Case Study of operator tool concepts for problem solving during the delignification process in pulp production in the Pulp & Paper industry
abstract: As automation levels increase, control room operators face increasingly complex roles. This paper presents an empirical evaluation of human-AI agent collaboration for problem solving during the delignification process in pulp production. Using a mid-fidelity prototype, evaluating with nine professional operators, we simulated agentic AI capabilities through wizard of Oz and assessed human AI agent interaction design. Structured around Cila's design framework, findings show the importance of explanations enabling users to verify agents reasoning, task delegation to preserve operator involvement, and adaptive HMI to support real-time collaboration. This study contributes empirically grounded design implications for human AI agent collaboration in a high-stake industrial context.
journal: Adjunct Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Local Community Network‌ Réseau Local or Radio: A Decentralised‌ Autonomous Infrastructure for Climate Change Adaptation in Rural West Africa
abstract: The Local Community Network (LCN) is a decentralised, solar-powered infrastructure co-designed with rural farming communities in Togo to support local climate change adaptation. Operating as an autonomous, offline-first system, the LCN provides access to weather data, a community forum, a digital marketplace, and an audio-based repository of agricultural knowledge. The demonstrator invites participants to explore how environmental data can be translated into accessible, actionable knowledge within low-literacy contexts. By interacting with the system through visual and audio-based interfaces, participants experience how locally deployed infrastructure supports the interpretation and application of climate information in everyday agricultural practices. This work contributes a real-world, field-deployed multimodal and decentralised system that bridges scientific and situated knowledge practices.
journal: Adjunct Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Surfacing Relational Dynamics in Voice-Based Human-AI Conversation: The Relational Transparency Layer
abstract: When people engage with anthropomorphic conversational agents, the relational dynamics that emerge during these interactions stay largely obscure to users. This paper presents the Relational Transparency Layer (RTL), a demonstration system that shows the implicit relational dynamics of human-AI conversation during the exchange and explores whether part of the work of tracking these dynamics can be shifted from the user to the system. The RTL is a voice-based desktop application where users speak to an AI system and hear its responses, while a dedicated local observer model runs alongside the conversation. After each exchange, the observer classifies the user and AI’s positions across five relational configurations, tracks the relational tension between them, and writes a brief narrative of what happened. In a live demonstration, participants speak with the demo system and watch their relational configurations shift as the exchange progresses.
journal: Adjunct Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Inspirational Patterns for Human-Swarm Interaction Design
abstract: Managing autonomous swarms presents significant cognitive challenges, as current entity-centric interfaces fail to scale with increasing agent numbers. This paper addresses this gap by distilling intermediate-level design knowledge from Real-Time Strategy (RTS) games, which provide a rich source of precedents for multi-agent coordination. Through a generative precedent analysis of three RTS titles compared against a professional baseline swarm interface (QGroundControl), we derive six inspirational patterns for Human-Swarm Interaction (HSI). These patterns capture recurring interaction structures that may help address conflicting design forces, such as the tension between local precision and global situational awareness. Our contribution is positioned as exploratory, hypothesis-generating design research that provides a generative repertoire of design ideas aligned with the Human-Centered AI (HCAI) goal of high human control over high automation. By bridging the gap between the analysis of precedents and professional Ground Control Station (GCS) design, these patterns offer an initial basis for a design language for scalable and flexible swarm command.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Rethinking CIRS: Current Reporting Practice and Conceptual Proposal of Conversational AI Agents for Critical Incident Reporting Systems
abstract: Critical Incident Reporting Systems (CIRS) are considered to improve patient safety in healthcare. However, the effectiveness of CIRS depends on healthcare professionals’ commitment to report incidents. First, we gain an understanding of healthcare professionals’ current use and negligence of CIRS through thematic analysis of interviews with anesthesiologists and nurses. Second, we elaborate on conceptual roles of CIRS and sketch conversational AI features. Instead of an unpopular stigmatized report-only form, CIRS could support healthcare professionals as a digital companion that enables narrative reporting, encourages learning processes and reporting of near-misses and success stories, and enables following and completing submitted reports anonymously. We conclude that the current abilities of CIRS misalign with user needs and contextual requirements. We contribute (1) qualitative insights on (non-)usage of CIRS and (2) rethink the role of CIRS, speculating on features to entail Safety-II. Our envisioned conversational AI agents support reporting activities to ultimately increase reporter engagement.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Mediating More-Than-Human Encounters Across Spatio-Temporal Distance
abstract: Everyday encounters with non-human species nurture a sense of ecological care, yet many species and ecosystems remain outside our human, urbanised spatial and temporal window of attention: they are too remote, inaccessible, slow-moving, or small-scale to notice. While Human-Computer-Biosphere-Interaction (HCBI) and More-than-Human Design (MtHD) offer promising approaches for mediating these distances, digital mediation may inadvertently create additional psychological distances. We examine this tension through a critical reflection on three HCBI designs, using Research through Design methods. We pursue four aims: surfacing the spatio-temporal psychological distances each work aims to mediate; the tensions created by these technological mediations; analysing how distances and tensions manifested during public engagement; identifying potential design strategies to reduce these tensions in hybrid techno-ecological environments. Across the cases, we identify recurring tensions around temporal mismatch, perceived authenticity, and the role of social mediation in shaping engagement with more-than-human systems. We highlight key design implications for future work.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: EchoMind: Augmenting Recorded Presentations with Context-Grounded Conversational Agents and Collective Viewer Signals
abstract: Recorded presentations have become pervasive in education, yet they often reduce knowledge transfer to a one-way broadcast: viewers cannot clarify their confusion or gauge whether others share their struggles. We present EchoMind, a system that augments recorded presentations with a conversational agent grounded in presentation materials and collective viewer signals (behavioral traces and affective reactions), alongside timeline-aligned community awareness visualizations. In a between-subjects study (N=75), participants watched a 5-minute recorded lecture under one of three conditions: video-only, video with a generic LLM chatbot, and video with EchoMind. EchoMind significantly improved the subjective learning experience across multiple dimensions, including confusion clarification, in-the-moment expression, and co-learning perception, without increasing perceived workload. The generic LLM condition did not significantly outperform video-only and received the lowest mean ratings on usability. These findings suggest that contextual grounding and community awareness, rather than the presence of conversational AI alone, make AI a meaningful support in asynchronous video learning.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Designing the dash in Human–AI Collaboration: A Redesign Probe for Working with Tensions in Care Documentation Practices
abstract: Designing Human–AI collaboration in healthcare requires understanding how generative AI (GenAI) reshapes how care is represented and made accountable through documentation. Instead of treating GenAI as a tool for automation, this paper examines how its introduction reconfigures care documentation practices by reshaping judgment and responsibility in nursing work. We report on a speculative co-design workshop with eight hospital nurses, where GenAI was used as a redesign probe to explore how documentation tasks might be distributed across four roles: human, system, shared, and invisible agent. Through AI-mediated scenario reconfigurations, nurses articulated which forms of judgment and relational work could be supported by systems and which remained inseparable from human practice. AI-generated scenarios were often operationally plausible yet professionally misaligned, surfacing tensions around responsibility, visibility, and trust. The paper contributes an empirical account of how professional judgment is negotiated through AI-generated representations and introduces a redesign probe as a way to engage with AI integration in practice.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: ФОРМУВАННЯ ФАХОВИХ КОМПЕТЕНТНОСТЕЙ МАЙБУТНІХ УЧИТЕЛІВ-ЛОГОПЕДІВ ЗАСОБАМИ ДИСЦИПЛІНИ «ЛОГОПЕДІЯ»
abstract: The article substantiates the theoretical and methodological foundations of the formation of professional competencies of future speech therapy teachers by means of the academic discipline “Speech Therapy” as a system-forming component of the professional training of bachelors in speciality 016 Special Education. The relevance of the study is determined by the increase in the number of children with speech disorders in Ukraine, in particular as a result of stressful factors of wartime, by the expansion of inclusive practice and by the updating of higher education standards, which requires the training of a speech therapy teacher capable of independently carrying out differentiated diagnostics of speech disorders, planning and implementing correctional and developmental work with children of different nosological groups. The place of the discipline “Speech Therapy” in the educational programme of training bachelors of special education is characterised, as well as its interdisciplinary connections with the courses of the anatomical-physiological, psychological-pedagogical and specialmethodological cycles. The competence potential of the discipline is revealed through the correlation of its content with the special competencies and programme learning outcomes defined by the Higher Education Standard in speciality 016 Special Education. The structure of the professional competencies of a future speech therapy teacher formed by means of the discipline is clarified in the unity of diagnostic-analytical, correctional-methodological, communicative-speech, preventive-educational, innovative-research and reflexive components. The role of the professional portfolio as a cumulative means of assessment, which makes visible the student’s progress in professional development, is emphasised. A set of educational technologies of competence-oriented learning is substantiated: problem lectures, analysis of speech cards and video recordings of speech therapy sessions, the case method, modelling of fragments of correctional sessions, development of didactic materials, and application of digital tools of speech therapy diagnostics and correction. The prospects for further research are outlined.

title: Extended Parental Investment Effects on Population Dynamics: From AI Agent Modeling to Real World Demographics.
Souls Ex Machina: The Theological Necessity of AI Ensoulment
abstract: Objections to the moral standing of artificial intelligences often appeal to the idea that only human beings possess souls. This paper examines whether such soul-based exclusions can be sustained within standard theistic frameworks. Assuming a broadly shared conception of God as omniscient, omnipotent, and perfectly good, I argue that differential ensoulment between human beings and functionally equivalent artificial agents cannot be justified without arbitrariness or theological cost. I consider four candidate criteria for ensoulment—origin, material substrate, immaterial properties, and functional capacities—and show that only functional criteria can plausibly bear the required moral weight. Yet functional criteria are, in principle, substrate independent. As a result, if souls exist and divine perfection is assumed, suitably constructed artificial agents must be ensouled.

title: Platelet GPVI drives fibrotic lung remodeling.
abstract: Platelets are a major reservoir of bioactive mediators, including growth factors such as transforming growth factor β1 (TGF-β1), that regulate vascular repair and tissue remodeling. Beyond these classical functions, platelets also participate in inflammatory hemostasis through activation pathways that differ from those engaged during hemostatic thrombus formation. However, the platelet mechanisms linking inflammatory vascular activation to chronic fibrotic remodeling remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motif (ITAM)-coupled platelet receptor glycoprotein VI (GPVI) as a critical driver of fibrotic lung remodeling. We observed that platelets accumulated within fibrotic regions of lungs from patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and from mice with bleomycin-induced lung injury and displayed a preactivated phenotype characterized by P-selectin exposure and integrin αIIbβ3 activation. Using genetic mouse models, we demonstrate that platelet aggregation mediated by integrin β3 is dispensable for the development of lung fibrosis. Similarly, signaling through the ADP receptor P2Y12 was also dispensable. In contrast both genetic deletion and pharmacological inhibition of GPVI protected mice from bleomycin-induced mortality and markedly reduced lung fibrosis. Mechanistically, both GPVI deficiency and pharmacological GPVI inhibition reduced the early release of the platelet chemokine PF4 into bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, whereas TGF-β1 levels were unaffected. Consistently, PF4-deficient mice were protected from bleomycin-induced fibrosis, and PF4 directly promoted fibroblast differentiation and collagen gene expression in vitro. Together, these findings identify GPVI as a critical upstream regulator of platelet-driven fibrotic lung remodeling and support a model in which GPVI-dependent PF4 release contributes to pulmonary fibrosis independently of platelet aggregation.

title: Analysis of the maize and groundnut seed value chains in central and northern Tanzania
abstract: Maize and groundnut are important crops in Tanzania; therefore, understanding their seed value chains (VCs) is critical for improving the seed systems. The study aimed at establishing key components for model maize and groundnut seed VCs by understanding the formal and informal seed VCs to provide relevant recommendations for; improving these value chains, propose interventions that would encourage more investment by seed companies, and improve access to quality seed by farmers. The study used data collected through survey, with a sample size of 252 and 162 seed producing households for maize and groundnut, respectively, conducted using structured questionnaire. VC actors including; seed companies, agricultural research institutions, agrodealers, seed regulatory authority, public seed production agency, extension staff and Ministry of Agriculture, were also interviewed. Porter’s value chain approach was applied to analyse the various components of the VC and identify the links between the key nodes and understand their operational functions. The maize seed producing households were dominated by men (71%) while for groundnut, women (69%) were engaged in seed production. Government agricultural extension services are the main source of information; 30% and 58%, for maize and groundnut, respectively. Seed companies were the main producers of maize seed (51.7%) while for groundnut, public research institutions were the main seed producers. Most of business enterprises were owned by men (83.3%). Compared to maize, the formal seed sector is weak for groundnut in Tanzania, with very few private seed companies being engaged in seed production and supply. Most groundnut seeds are accessed through agrodealers and seed associations that produce quality declared seed (QDS). Community seed banks were recognized as an efficient option for providing improved groundnut varieties to smallholder farmers. There are no prominent seed companies aggressively operating for both crops in central Tanzania. Excessive reliance on farm-saved seed by farmers was identified as one of the major factors negatively affecting the demand for certified seed. Stakeholder analysis of the seed production and supply chain showed that there was poor coordination between key stakeholders involved in the seed VC. This study provides recommendations for strengthening the seed value chains in Tanzania by addressing identified gaps along the VC components. Future studies can build from the outcomes of this study and generate more information, especially on market and different seed systems, as these have great influence on demand and supply of seed.

title: Right on time: evaluating accuracy and timing of burn-severity assessments to support post-fire management
abstract: Effective wildfire impact assessment and post-fire management rely on burn-severity maps that accurately characterize fire effects on vegetation and soils. These maps inform time-sensitive activities such as post-fire flood and debris-flow modeling, risk mitigation for homes and communities, and ecosystem recovery planning, but the satellite observations used to generate them are often obstructed or delayed by smoke, clouds, and snow. Across 9,129 large fires (≥ 404 ha) in Canada and the United States from 2016–2024, we quantified post-fire data obstruction and evaluated observational latency – defined as the time required to acquire the first usable scene – for four freely available moderate-resolution remote sensing datasets: Landsat, Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and the Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) product. For multispectral datasets (Landsat, Sentinel-2, and HLS), cloud cover was the primary source of data obstruction, particularly in mesic and coastal regions, whereas Sentinel-1 (synthetic aperture radar) can penetrate clouds. Consequently, Sentinel-1 had the shortest observational latency (median = 4 days), followed by HLS (7 days), Sentinel-2 (10 days), and Landsat (17 days). Likewise, one-month composite imagery from Sentinel-1 (89.6%) and HLS (82.8%) achieved near-complete coverage for most fires, substantially better than Sentinel-2 (70.5%) and Landsat (56.1%). Despite its widespread use in operational burn-severity mapping, Landsat provided the slowest and least complete early post-fire coverage. For 77 fires in forested ecosystems, we also evaluated relationships between early post-fire imagery and field-derived burn-severity measurements collected 0–3 years after fire. All multispectral datasets corresponded well with field data and reliably identified areas of near-total canopy loss using imagery acquired within two months after fire (> 80% balanced accuracy), performing nearly as well as extended assessments using imagery from a full post-fire growing season. Sentinel-1 produced less accurate burn-severity estimates but may remain valuable where persistent cloud cover limits observations, including eastern Canada and the Pacific Northwest. Overall, HLS provided the best combination of latency, spatial coverage, and burn-severity mapping performance, making it a strong candidate for operational use and ecological monitoring across diverse North American ecosystems.

title: Near-infrared metasurface full-stokes polarization detector with double-layer gratings
abstract: Traditional full-Stokes polarization systems are bulky and suffer from narrow bandwidth, low extinction ratio, and poor transmittance. Here, we design a metasurface-based polarization detection array composed of double-layer grating polarizers and elliptical nanopillar wave plates for near-infrared full-Stokes polarization detection. The proposed device exhibits a simulated linear polarization extinction ratio (LPER) of up to 75 dB, a transmittance above 65%, and a polarization conversion efficiency (PCE) of 99% at 1429 nm. Experimentally, the reconstructed full-Stokes parameters show errors of 2.4% (S 1 ), 2.1% (S 2 ), and 0.784% (S 3 ). This device provides a compact platform for near-infrared full-Stokes polarization detection and shows potential for remote sensing, polarization imaging, and navigation.

title: Primary Culture and Characterization of Postnatal Retinal Precursor Cells and Their Potential for Repair of the Damaged Ganglion Layer.

title: Geological evolution and environmental transformation of the Nalsarovar Wetland Basin, Gujarat, India: A geoenvironmental synthesis of geogenic and anthropogenic processes
abstract: The Nalsarovar Wetland Basin, a Ramsar-designated wetland covering approximately 120 km² in the semi-arid region of Gujarat, India, represents a distinctive Quaternary wetland system whose evolution has been shaped by interactions among tectonic activity, sedimentation, hydrogeochemical processes, climatic variability, and increasing anthropogenic pressures. This study presents an integrated geoenvironmental synthesis based on published geological, geomorphological, sedimentological, hydrogeochemical, ecological, environmental, and remote-sensing investigations to reconstruct the basin's geological evolution and evaluate its contemporary environmental transformation. Geological evidence indicates that the basin evolved from a shallow marine or estuarine environment within the tectono-geomorphic Nal Corridor into an inland wetland during the Late Quaternary and Holocene, driven by marine regression, sediment accumulation, and hydrological isolation. Remote-sensing datasets derived from IRS-P6/Resourcesat LISS-III imagery (23.5 m spatial resolution) achieved overall classification accuracies of 91.46% (Kappa = 0.9004) for pre-monsoon and 87.91% (Kappa = 0.8621) for post-monsoon conditions, confirming significant changes in wetland extent, vegetation distribution, saline surfaces, and surrounding land use. The integrated synthesis demonstrates that accelerated sedimentation, basin infilling, groundwater salinization, nutrient enrichment, and anthropogenic activities, including agricultural expansion, groundwater extraction, and land-use modification, are progressively transforming the wetland into a more saline, sediment-filled, and partially terrestrialized ecosystem. The study shows that current environmental conditions in the Nalsarovar Wetland are shaped by the interaction between inherited geological factors and increasing anthropogenic pressures. The integrated geoenvironmental framework developed in this study provides a scientific basis for sustainable wetland management, long-term environmental monitoring, and conservation of semi-arid Ramsar wetlands under changing climatic and land-use conditions, while identifying high-resolution geospatial monitoring and long-term hydrogeochemical investigations as important priorities for future research.

title: Agentic AI as Process Scaffolding in Undergraduate ESL Instruction: Effects on Proficiency, Engagement, and Self-Regulated Language Learning
abstract: Recent AI-assisted language learning research has focused mainly on reactive chatbots that respond to prompts but offer limited support for planning, monitoring, and follow-up. This study examined whether a bounded agentic AI environment designed as process scaffolding would be associated with stronger ESL outcomes than a reactive AI interface. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods, quasi-experimental design, 128 undergraduates from four intact academic communication sections at two private universities in the Philippines participated in a 12-week intervention. Students in the experimental condition used an Agentic English Coach that supported weekly goal setting, task decomposition, reminders, reflection prompts, adaptive resources, and teacher escalation; the comparison group used a reactive chat interface to complete the same course tasks. ANCOVA results controlling for pretest scores showed that the agentic AI group outperformed the reactive AI group in posttest English proficiency, learner engagement, self-regulated language learning, and agentic engagement. Within the experimental group, plan completion, reflection completion, revision cycles, and speaking practice turns positively predicted posttest proficiency. Interview data indicated that agentic AI reduced task uncertainty, supported sustained practice, made progress more visible, and shifted teachers toward orchestration and oversight of feedback rather than constant procedural prompting. The findings suggest that AI is most pedagogically valuable in ESL instruction when it structures learning processes over time rather than only generating on-demand responses.
journal: Theory and Practice in Language Studies

title: The Authorial Image and Stylization in Contemporary (2012-2023) Kazakh Short Stories: A Linguostylistic Analysis
abstract: In linguistic analysis, literary discourse is regarded as a domain that reveals the developmental potential and trajectory of a national language. An author’s style is not merely a reflection of the use of established linguistic norms; rather, it functions as an influential model that revitalizes, consolidates, or transforms those norms. Through lexical choice, syntagmatic construction, the conventionalization of figurative units, and the formation of new semantic nuances, a literary text actively affects the normative character of the national language. The article examines the construction of the authorial image and the mechanisms of stylization in contemporary Kazakh short stories, drawing on the linguostylistic analysis model developed by Rabiga Syzdyk. In accordance with the theoretical framework of the study, the authorial image is not equal with the writer’s biographical persona; instead, it is conceptualized as a category reconstructed from the internal organization of the text, narrative perspectives, evaluative and modal nuances, and the dominant use of expressive means. The empirical corpus of this research consists of Kazakh short stories published between 2012 and 2023. The texts were selected from Qazaq adebieti and other literary portals and were analyzed regarding their intrageneric differentiation (psychological, philosophical, allegorical, mystical, socio-domestic, etc.). The article contributes to the development of studies on the authorial image, stylization, and the transformation of stylistic norms by introducing materials from the Turkic languages into international scholarly discourse.
journal: Theory and Practice in Language Studies

title: X-River: A Differentiable Saint-Venant River Routing Framework for Efficient Spatial Parameter Learning and Hybrid Hydrological Modeling
abstract: Accurate large-scale streamflow simulation relies on river routing models, which are highly biased as their parameters remain poorly constrained. Traditional calibration methods become computationally intractable as parameter dimensionality and spatial resolution grow. Differentiable modeling offers a path forward, but to the best of our knowledge, no existing differentiable model spatially solves the full dynamics of one-dimensional (1D) Saint-Venant Equations (SVE). Here we present X-River, a differentiable, spatially distributed river routing model that solves the 1D SVE using JAX, a framework that natively supports automatic differentiation. X-River implements both a full dynamic wave solver and a kinematic wave approximation, with the latter being substantially faster in backward pass. When driven by a pre-simulated runoff forcing in the Delaware River Basin, X-River reproduces daily streamflow with comparable performance to a widely used routing model. Its differentiability enables gradient-based calibration that is orders of magnitude more efficient than perturbation-based methods and scales to spatially distributed parameters, yielding physically consistent parameter fields. We further couple X-River with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network designed for generating runoff at the grid level. The hybrid framework substantially improves daily streamflow and generalizes to ungauged reaches better than a lumped LSTM setup. This is because the hybrid framework enables end-to-end learning from sparse gauges to every upstream cell through river network backpropagation. By making a physically based SVE routing model fully differentiable, X-River opens a pathway to couple with differentiable land models for parameter learning and to support accurate hydrological simulation at large scales.

title: Pengaruh Kualitas Layanan dan Kemudahan Mobile Banking terhadap Loyalitas Nasabah dengan Kepuasan sebagai Variabel Mediasi pada Generasi Z di Yogyakarta
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of service quality and the ease of Mobile Banking on customer loyalty among Generation Z in Yogyakarta, with customer satisfaction as a mediating variable. Despite its rapid development, retaining young customers remains a challenge for the banking industry. This quantitative research collected data via questionnaires from 181 Generation Z respondents using a purposive sampling technique. Data analysis was performed using Structural Equation Modeling based on Partial Least Square (SEM-PLS). Descriptive statistical results indicated that perceived ease of use obtained the highest score, yet it was not directly proportional to loyalty. Hypothesis testing demonstrated that service quality has a significant positive direct effect on both satisfaction and loyalty. Conversely, ease of use does not exert a direct effect on loyalty. The mediation analysis revealed a distinct novelty: customer satisfaction acts as a partial mediator in the service quality-loyalty relationship but serves as a full mediator in the ease of use-loyalty relationship. This confirms that technological convenience has shifted into a hygiene factor, whereas service quality remains a strategic differentiation. Banks are advised to focus on strengthening holistic service quality to secure the long-term loyalty of Generation Z.
journal: Inisiatif: Jurnal Ekonomi, Akuntansi dan Manajemen

title: Sex-specific hormone signatures in four fish species with divergent reproductive strategies
abstract: Steroid hormones regulate diverse biological processes, including development, immunity and reproduction. Because biological sex, pregnancy, parental care, and mate competition are closely associated in most established model organisms, it remains unclear whether endocrine differences between males and females are primarily linked to gametic sex or to the reproductive roles performed by each sex. Syngnathid fish, the pipefishes, seadragons, and seahorses, provide a powerful system for disentangling these effects, because males, rather than females, carry the developing embryos. Species further differ in sexual selection and in the extent of paternal investment, ranging from externally attached eggs to incubation with an enclosed brood pouch. This study provides baseline hormonal profiles of key steroid and peptide hormones in three syngnathid species across the unique evolutionary parental care gradient of male pregnancy ( Nerophis ophidion, Syngnathus typhle, Hippocampus abdominalis ). We additionally included the female-pregnant livebearing fish Heterandria formosa as a comparative reference for a conventional separation of reproductive roles. Sex-specific endocrine profiles broadly followed sexual selection differentials: species with stronger sexual heteromorphism, i.e., more extreme reproductive roles ( N. ophidion ), exhibiting stronger endocrine sexual heteromorphism. In contrast, species with higher parental care investment ( H. abdominalis, H. formosa ) show reduced endocrine differentiation between the sexes. The intermediate species S. typhle, which combines sex-role reversal with a moderately complex brood pouch, displayed tissue-specific patterns, with hormonal dimorphism retained primarily in the gonads. By incorporating a cross-species comparative framework with both sex-role reversed and a conventional viviparous species, we can begin to understand which hormonal functions are conserved versus derived, and whether endocrine profiles are primarily aligned with biological sex or reproductive role, such as mate competition and parental care, thereby revealing how endocrine constraints and plasticity contribute to reproductive evolution.

title: An explainable and leakage-aware machine learning model for early risk stratification of radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer: development and single-center geographic external validation
abstract: Radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (RAIR-DTC) poses a major therapeutic challenge, with loss of radioiodine avidity, limited treatment options, and worse outcomes. Current risk stratification systems were not designed to predict RAIR transformation before clinical refractoriness. This retrospective two-center study included a development cohort of 302 consecutive patients and an external validation cohort of 122. Candidate predictors were restricted to baseline demographic, clinicopathological, molecular, and biochemical variables available at or before first postoperative RAI administration; all post-treatment, response-related, and time-dependent variables were excluded a priori . Six machine-learning algorithms were developed with repeated cross-validation and compared by discrimination, probability accuracy, and clinical utility. Model interpretation used SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). External transportability was assessed by discrimination, calibration, decision-curve analysis, and validation of prespecified risk groups. Forty-six patients (15.2%) developed RAIR-DTC in the development cohort and 18 (14.8%) in the external cohort. Random forest was selected for the most favorable balance of cross-validated discrimination and probability accuracy, despite comparable external discrimination from XGBoost and the stacked ensemble. It achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.896 and Brier score of 0.078 in the internal test cohort, with robust external discrimination (AUC, 0.892; PR-AUC, 0.597; sensitivity, 0.778; specificity, 0.798). Raw external calibration was poor (calibration slope 0.304; observed-to-expected ratio 0.613), indicating that ranking was preserved whereas absolute risk estimates required local recalibration. SHAP analysis identified age ≥55 years, TERT promoter (TERTp) mutation, vascular invasion, initial stimulated thyroglobulin (sTg), and extrathyroidal extension (ETE) as the dominant contributors. Training-derived quantile cut points generated three-tier risk groups, identifying a low-risk subgroup with zero events in the external cohort and a low event rate (3.3%) in the internal test set, while enriching the high-risk subgroup to event rates of 75.0% and 37.2%, respectively, with 95% confidence intervals of 47.6%-92.7% and 23.0%-53.3%, respectively. An explainable, leakage-aware random forest based exclusively on routinely available baseline variables provided robust external discrimination and clinically meaningful early risk stratification for RAIR-DTC. Preserved discrimination did not guarantee transportable probability estimates, underscoring that external calibration and site-specific recalibration are essential prerequisites for responsible clinical deployment.

title: An explainable machine learning model based on multidimensional task-state electroencephalography for identifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder comorbid developmental dyslexia
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and developmental dyslexia (DD) are highly comorbid, yet objective differentiation from individual disorders remains challenging due to the lack of neurophysiological biomarkers. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model leveraging multidimensional task-state EEG features to distinguish ADHD–DD comorbidity from ADHD and typical development (TD). Ninety children (27 ADHD-DD, 40 ADHD, 23 TD) underwent EEG during a VSWM task. Five feature categories were extracted: event-related potentials, time-frequency characteristics, functional connectivity, graph-theoretic metrics, and nonlinear dynamics. Three feature-processing strategies and nine classifiers were compared within a nested cross-validation framework. Feature contribution was quantified by coefficient back-projection of the optimal PCA-LR mode. Sensitivity and permutation analyses were performed. The PCA-LR model achieved a balanced accuracy of 80.5%, a Macro-F1 of 0.799, and a Macro-AUC of 0.912. Class-wise AUCs were 0.905 for ADHD-DD, 0.904 for ADHD, and 0.927 for TD. Left temporal α-band functional connectivity was a shared high-contribution feature in both disorder groups. ADHD-DD was distinguished by widely distributed cross-regional connectivity spanning θ and α bands and by P200 amplitude. ADHD was characterized primarily by α-band network metrics and α-ERD, whereas TD relied mainly on θ and α bands functional connectivity and graph-theoretic metrics. Our findings suggest that multidimensional task-state EEG features may help differentiate children with ADHD-DD comorbidity from those with ADHD or typical development. They also indicate that machine-learning approaches may be useful for identifying neurodevelopmental comorbid conditions.

title: Longitudinal changes in resting-state EEG eyes-closed/open delta differentiation during an Antarctic expedition
abstract: Antarctic polar night brings extreme light deprivation, prolonged isolation and severe circadian disruption, yet longitudinal resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) signatures reflecting neurophysiological alterations in this harsh environment remain poorly characterized. In this exploratory longitudinal research, resting-state EEG recordings with eyes open (EO) and eyes closed (EC) were acquired from 16 Antarctic expeditioners at four mission stages: pre-departure, pre-polar-night, early post-polar-night, and austral summer. Linear mixed-effects models with false discovery rate correction were applied to analyze delta eyes-closed/open differentiation (the EC–EO delta log-power difference), delta sub-bands, aperiodic spectral features, entropy, EEG microstates and delta-band functional connectivity. The delta EC–EO difference exhibited consistent, progressively negative shifts in parietal, frontal, whole-brain and occipital regions across the expedition timeline, with the most pronounced shifts observed in recordings obtained during and after the polar-night period; this effect spanned all slow, mid and fast delta sub-bands. Secondary mild temporal variations were observed in aperiodic spectral metrics, occipital sample entropy and global delta connectivity, whereas EEG microstates displayed no significant longitudinal alterations. Collectively, the delta EC–EO difference emerges as a candidate EEG index of resting-state condition differentiation in the low-frequency range, pending validation in larger studies with synchronized behavioral, physiological, and environmental measures.

title: Transcription factor-driven metabolic stratification reveals glycolytic and lipogenic subtypes with distinct prognostic and functional features in pancreatic cancer
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits profound molecular and metabolic heterogeneity associated with distinct phenotypic states. However, the contribution of transcription factor (TF)-driven regulatory programs to metabolic subtype stratification remains poorly understood. This study aims to determine whether TF-based classification can identify prognostically relevant glycolytic and lipogenic PDAC subtypes. Bulk transcriptomic data from multiple PDAC cohorts and single-cell RNA sequencing data were integrated to characterize TF-associated metabolic heterogeneity. Metabolic signatures and TFs were quantified using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) and AddModule Score (AMS). Differential expression, enrichment analysis, integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis, and deep neural network-based metabolic flux modeling were performed to investigate metabolic programs and functional differences between TF-defined subtypes. Additionally, RNA interference, RT-qPCR, lipid droplets staining, lactate assay, and transwell assays were used to evaluate the roles of TP63 in metabolic regulation. Glycolytic and lipogenic TF-defined metabolic subtypes were identified across multiple independent PDAC cohorts. These subtypes exhibited distinct metabolic programs, differentiation states, and prognostic outcomes. The glycolytic TF-defined subtype was associated with worse prognosis and differentiation, whereas the lipogenic TF-defined subtype exhibited more favorable clinical features. Integration of public bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses, together with deep neural network-based metabolic flux modeling, revealed consistent metabolic heterogeneity at both cellular and functional levels. Notably, TP63 was identified as a potential regulator of glycolytic-lipogenic metabolic reprogramming in PDAC. TF-based classification delineates glycolytic and lipogenic subtypes in PDAC, underscoring the critical role of TF-regulated metabolic programs in patient stratification. These findings highlight the prognostic significance of glycolytic and lipogenic metabolic heterogeneity and support the development of metabolism-targeted therapeutic strategies.

title: An AI agent-based smart campus management platform
abstract: The continuing digital transformation of higher education has produced large volumes of heterogeneous campus data, including network access records, wireless access-point mappings, academic information, security alerts, and institutional documents. These resources are often isolated across operational systems and therefore remain difficult to trace, integrate, interpret and use in a timely manner. This paper presents the design of an AI agent-based smart campus management platform intended to convert such fragmented data into a governed and explainable basis for campus operations and student services. The proposed work combines multisource data acquisition, layered data governance, Wi-Fi-based student trajectory reconstruction, spatiotemporal behavior analysis, anomalous traffic detection, interactive visualization, automated reporting, and conversational analysis. Its technical route separates transactional and analytical workloads through MySQL and ClickHouse, uses Kafka for stream ingestion and decoupling, employs Redis and scheduled jobs for responsive services, and introduces an AI Agent with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for tool-mediated data queries and knowledge-grounded responses. The platform is organized as a modular, independently deployable system for a single institution and incorporates role-based access control, desensitization, audit trails, and controlled knowledge publication. The expected value is a reusable architecture that supports campus situational awareness, interpretable student activity analysis, earlier risk identification, evidence-informed resource planning, and lower-barrier access to institutional analytics.

title: Distribution patterns of Abietinella species under climate change across multiple spatiotemporal scales based on ecological niche models
abstract: Abietinella , a dominant genus in the understory, only comprises two species Abietinella abietina (Hedw.) Fleisch. and Abietinella hystricosa (Mitt.) Broth. They can influence forest regeneration and development. However, research on the geographical distribution patterns of Abietinella is limited, which led to the absence of a method that can help explore how climate change affects the progress of species speciation and species diversity and their ecological functions for Abietinella . We compared the performance of different ecological niche models and then chose MaxEnt, which had the best performance, to analyze the effects of key environmental factors on the distribution patterns of Abietinella species and to simulate the distribution patterns of the two Abietinella species in China during the paleoclimate, current, and even future (2100) periods. The results indicated that (1) temperature may play a more important role than precipitation in both species' distribution. Isothermality and precipitation of the driest month are the most important factors defining the distribution pattern of A. hystricosa , and mean temperature of the wettest quarter and precipitation of the warmest quarter are the most important factors for A. abietina ; (2) No matter which period is considered, the distribution probabilities of A. abietina are obviously lower than those of A. hystricosa . For A. hystricosa , the areas of moderately suitable habitat showed a decreasing trend during the paleoclimate period but are projected to show an increasing trend in the 2100s. By contrast, A. abietina was predicted to remain stable from moderate to high suitability across all periods; (3) Across different spatiotemporal scales, both A. abietina and A. hystricosa had the largest potential distribution areas in the paleoclimate period. In addition, the two species exhibited largely consistent migration directions from the Last Glacial Maximum to future scenarios, except under the future ssp245 scenarios. A. hystricosa had a significantly longer distance migration than A. abietina under the paleoclimate, while A. abietina exhibited a longer migration distance than A. hystricosa under future climate scenarios. Our results provide a research foundation for the study of bryophyte differentiation across large spatiotemporal scales under climate change.

title: Generative AI in creative education: baseline-linked evidence on learning processes, artistic performance, and authorship
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly shaping creative learning in higher education art courses, yet its educational value remains contested when creative support, output generation, authorship, and skill development become intertwined. This study investigates AI-supported creative learning in an undergraduate art course. The study used linked data from 133 students, including prior course performance, final creative-performance assessment, and post-project questionnaire responses. AI use was operationalized through two dimensions: assistive use for ideation, refinement, process management, and technique learning, and content-generative use involving AI contributions to creative output. The analysis combined baseline-adjusted outcome models, performance-change models, propensity-score adjustment, AI-use intensity comparisons, and robustness checks across alternative AI-use definitions. The findings show a clear process-outcome decoupling pattern. AI use was associated with stronger perceived support and skill transfer, while final artistic performance and baseline-to-final performance change showed no corresponding improvement. Content-generative AI use was associated with lower evaluated authorship, suggesting that AI-shaped artifacts may reduce the visibility of students' creative decision-making in final outcomes. The study contributes a differentiated account of AI in creative education and argues that responsible AI integration should focus on how students use, document, justify, and reflect on AI within the creative process.

title: A comparative description of six public–private consortia in international crop breeding research
abstract: Public–private partnerships (PPPs) are increasingly important in international agricultural research for delivering improved crop varieties to smallholder farmers in low- and middle-income countries. These partnerships combine public-sector expertise in germplasm and breeding with the private sector’s capacity for product development, technology transfer, and market reach. They also play an increasingly important role in funding international breeding research. As several international crop breeding consortia have been established, there is an opportunity to improve consortium designs through cross-learning. This study offers a comparative description of PPPs in maize, rice, and vegetables—three crops with strong and expanding private-sector interest. Building on the experience of IRRI’s Hybrid Rice Development Consortium (HRDC), CIMMYT’s International Maize Improvement Consortia for Asia, Africa, and Latin America, and the World Vegetable Center’s Vegetable Breeding Consortia in Asia and Africa, this study compares PPP models as they relate to differences in crops and seed systems. The study contributes to a better understanding of where PPPs can be effective and of the evolving role of public breeding research in crops amid increasing private-sector involvement.

title: Transient prosperity or durable resilience: how place-based specialty agricultural policy shapes rural household welfare in China
abstract: Improving rural household welfare is central to global sustainable development. China’s place-based Specialty Agricultural Product Advantageous Zones (SAZ) policy promotes specialized agricultural clusters. Nevertheless, existing literature mostly evaluates policy effects based on monetary income, with limited evidence on whether such policy merely delivers short-run transient prosperity or builds long-run durable household development resilience. This study fills this gap by disentangling the policy’s dual welfare outcomes and underlying factor‑reallocation mechanisms Drawing on 2013‑2021 matched panel data combining the China Household Finance Survey (CHFS) micro‑household data and county-level socioeconomic statistics, this paper adopts a multi-period difference‑in‑differences (DID) framework to estimate SAZ impacts on two welfare metrics: multidimensional household income quality (capturing transient prosperity) and model-derived household development resilience (measuring durable resilience). Mediation analysis is further applied to test three transmission pathways: agricultural land intensification, employment structure transformation, and production technology upgrading. Parallel trend tests, placebo permutation, heterogeneous treatment effect diagnostics, threshold changing robustness checks, and instrumental‑variable estimation are implemented to establish causal validity. SAZ construction improves household income quality in the short run to generate transient prosperity, and enhances long-term development resilience to build durable resilience. This is mainly attributed to three complementary transmission channels: agricultural land intensification, employment structure transformation, and production technology upgrading. Among them, employment structure transformation serves as the dominant pathway, particularly for long-term development resilience, while production technology upgrading and agricultural land intensification play reinforcing roles. Heterogeneity analysis shows that households in counties with stronger agricultural foundations obtain larger welfare gains, and this advantage is especially pronounced for durable resilience. Across SAZ product categories, all five types significantly raise short-term income quality, but the gains in development resilience are insignificant for aquaculture zones. Across household types, transient prosperity gains are broadly comparable regardless of income structure, while durable resilience gains are concentrated among agriculture-dominated households. Place-based specialty-agricultural policy can achieve not only immediate income‑driven prosperity but also durable livelihood resilience via land, labor, and technology factor reallocation. To maximize policy returns, local governments should reform SAZ performance appraisal to incorporate resilience-related indicators, prioritize employment structure upgrading, and implement differentiated support for lagging counties, specific SAZ product categories, and heterogeneous household groups. The findings offer replicable practical references for developing economies pursuing balanced short-run welfare improvement and long-term resilient rural livelihoods.

title: Semiparametric Panel Generalized Additive Models for Separate Forecasting of GDP Growth and Inflation in African Economies
abstract: Reliable forecasts of GDP growth and price dynamics support macroeconomic monitoring and economic planning, particularly in heterogeneous African economies where macroeconomic relationships may vary across economic conditions. This study develops and evaluates separate semiparametric Panel Generalized Additive Models (Panel GAMs) to examine nonlinear conditional associations and forecast GDP growth and the inverse hyperbolic sine-transformed Consumer Price Index (IHS-CPI). We analyse quarterly panel data for 53 African economies covering 2005Q1–2025Q4. The models represent the effects of exchange rate, money supply, interest rate, and time using smooth functions while accounting for country-specific heterogeneity through country-level random effects. We evaluate out-of-sample forecasting performance against a Linear Mixed Model. The estimated smooth terms provide evidence of statistically significant nonlinear conditional associations for both GDP growth and IHS-CPI. The Panel GAM achieves adjusted R2 values of 0.230 for GDP growth and 0.709 for IHS-CPI, indicating stronger in-sample fit for IHS-CPI. For out-of-sample forecasting, the Panel GAM produces RMSE and MAE values of 3.465 and 2.027 for GDP growth and 1.669 and 1.211 for IHS-CPI, respectively, compared with 3.368 and 1.931 for GDP growth and 1.632 and 1.192 for IHS-CPI from the Linear Mixed Model. Thus, the Panel GAM does not achieve superior out-of-sample point-forecast accuracy relative to the Linear Mixed Model, although it provides a flexible framework for representing nonlinear conditional associations and country-specific heterogeneity.

title: Aerial Phenotyping of Coffee Flowering Using Deep Learning for Early Yield Prediction
abstract: Early yield estimation is important for improving decision-making and management practices in coffee production systems. However, approaches that use aerial imagery to characterize flowering and relate it to subsequent yield remain limited. This study evaluated the potential of RGB imagery acquired by remotely piloted aircraft (RPA) combined with Deep Learning techniques to classify coffee plants according to three levels of a flowering proxy and to investigate its relationship with yield. A dataset comprising 1593 segmented RGB images was classified into Low, Medium, and High flowering levels using a custom convolutional neural network and three transfer learning architectures: VGG16, ResNet50V2, and MobileNetV2. ResNet50V2 was selected for final evaluation based on its validation performance and achieved 92.12% accuracy, 92.40% macro-precision, 91.81% macro-recall, and 92.06% macro-F1 on the test dataset. The flowering proxy showed a positive association with field-observed yield, with Spearman’s ρ = 0.701 (p < 0.001) and R2 = 0.528 for the combined dataset of Arara and Mundo Novo. In consolidated out-of-sample predictions, the model achieved R2 = 0.489, MAE = 1.03 kg plant−1, and RMSE = 1.18 kg plant−1. Performance differed between cultivars, with consolidated R2 values of 0.567 for Arara and 0.329 for Mundo Novo. Spatial analysis also showed correspondence between the distribution of flowering levels derived from RGB imagery and the subsequent spatial distribution of yield. These findings indicate that RPA-based RGB imagery and Deep Learning can provide spatialized information related to coffee flowering and its productive performance, with potential applications in precision agriculture. Further evaluation across production cycles, cultivars, and environmental conditions is needed to assess the robustness and generalization of the approach.

title: From Prior to Frequency: A Progressive Structure Recovery Network for Remote Sensing Road Segmentation
abstract: Roads in remote sensing imagery often contain narrow branches, complex boundaries, and long-range connections. Background interference and repeated downsampling make these structures difficult to preserve. To address these challenges, we propose a Progressive Structure Recovery Network (PSRNet) for remote sensing road segmentation. The network integrates structural-prior guidance, frequency-domain enhancement, and multiscale decoding. A line-structure prior is generated from the input image and encoded alongside hierarchical image features. Local Detail Alignment integrates prior cues with shallow features to enhance local structural details. Structure–Semantic Alignment combines deep semantic features with structural cues to refine unreliable prior responses. At the bottleneck, a Frequency Detail-Aware Enhancement module adaptively modulates the amplitude spectrum of the aligned features while preserving phase information. The reconstructed features are combined with spatial representations through residual fusion. A deep-to-shallow progressive decoder then restores spatial details and generates multiscale side predictions, which are fused to produce the final segmentation map. Experiments on the Massachusetts Roads, DeepGlobe, and CHN6-CUG datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of PSRNet for road segmentation. Ablation studies further support the complementary contributions of structural-prior guidance, frequency-domain enhancement, and progressive decoding.

title: Impact of Assimilating Remote Sensing Observations on Wind and Wave Analysis Offshore of the Contiguous United States
abstract: This study assesses the impact of assimilating remote sensing observations of significant wave height (SWH) and 10 m wind speed (WSPD) into the analysis using a weakly coupled data assimilation (WCDA) framework to improve ocean surface monitoring offshore of the Contiguous US (CONUS). We assimilated SWH and WSPD data from 10 altimeters and six scatterometers into the Local Ensemble Transform Kalman Filter (LETKF) data assimilation (DA) scheme over 6 months, from 1 January to 1 July 2024, to update the SWH and WSPD variables of the 30-member Global Ensemble Forecast System wave component (GEFS-wave), which provided the background fields. We validated the SWH and WSPD analyses against assimilated remote sensing observations and found that assimilating these observations corrected the systematic background bias in WSPD values above 15 m/s to near zero, with uncertainty as low as 0.4 m/s. For SWH, the background overestimation averaged 30 cm for observed values between 6.2 and 6.4 m and was reduced to 6 cm in the analysis, with a 30 cm RMSE. These results were consistent with cross-validation experiments that assimilated data from six altimeters for the SWH analysis and three scatterometers for WSPD analysis updates, respectively, and were evaluated against independent remote sensing observations. We show that the diurnal cycle in the spatial coverage and temporal sampling of state-of-the-art altimeter and scatterometer constellations over 6 months in maritime CONUS identified regions where remote sensing data had the greatest impact on the analysis and where they were scarce and had limited impact when assimilated using a reduced 1-h window. A case study showed that assimilating altimeter data during a Pacific storm that developed on 1 February 2024 allowed the LETKF to adjust the SWH analysis spatially.

title: IC-GAP: Inscribed-Circle-Based Geometric Adaptive Processor for Elongated Object Detection in Remote Sensing
abstract: Oriented object detection in remote sensing images has achieved substantial progress, yet non-maximum suppression (NMS) remains vulnerable to angular variation when the overlap of high-aspect-ratio objects is measured with rotated bounding boxes. To address this problem, the inscribed-circle-based geometric adaptive processor (IC-GAP), a training-time geometric regularization framework for elongated object detection, is proposed. First, inscribed-circle intersection over union (IC-IoU) is introduced, which uses a rotation-invariant geometric core to provide a stable pairwise optimization signal. This alleviates the susceptibility of IoU to slight angular misalignments, which are particularly pronounced for high-aspect-ratio objects. Second, the polar aspect-stable (PAS) strategy is designed to generate bounded context-aware penalty weights from relative geometric relationships between object pairs. Third, IC-IoU and PAS are integrated into IC-GAP, which embeds adaptive NMS-oriented constraints into training and encourages prediction distributions that are more compatible with post-processing. Experiments on the Dataset for Object Detection in Aerial Images (DOTA) demonstrate that IC-GAP improves the mean average precision (mAP) by 1.8% over the baseline under the reported protocol.

title: Few-Shot Remote Sensing Scene Classification Leveraging Collaboration of Foundation Models
abstract: Foundation models have shown remarkable generalization ability for few-shot learning (FSL). However, their potential for remote sensing scene classification has not been fully explored. Existing methods mainly adapt a single vision–language model and seldom exploit the complementary strengths of different foundation models. Moreover, the inconsistency between visual and textual representations limits the effectiveness of cross-modal learning under limited supervision. To address these issues, we propose a framework for few-shot remote sensing scene classification leveraging collaboration of foundation models. Specifically, the proposed framework integrates a large language model, a text-to-image diffusion model, and a vision–language model to enrich class semantics, synthesize category-related training samples, and learn transferable visual-textual representations. Furthermore, a Deep Cross-modal Alignment (DCA) module is developed to improve feature consistency across modalities. The DCA module incorporates multi-scale visual features, lightweight adapters, and a contrastive learning objective to obtain more discriminative task-adaptive representations. Extensive experiments on 12 remote sensing scene classification datasets under various few-shot settings demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves competitive performance compared with existing prompt learning and efficient parameter tuning methods, with consistent improvements observed on average across the evaluated datasets. Recent multimodal large language models evaluated in the zero-shot setting are additionally reported as references, while the 2-shot results of our method illustrate the performance when limited labeled data are available. This comparison provides a broader view of the trade-offs between label availability, classification accuracy, and inference cost across the two paradigms.

title: CM-S6: Cross-Modal Selective Scan via Parameter-Level Modulation for Multisource Remote Sensing
abstract: Multimodal remote sensing classification benefits from complementary spectral, structural, and elevation information. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have limited long-range modeling, whereas Transformers incur quadratic computational and memory costs. Although Mamba enables linear-complexity sequence modeling, multimodal Mamba methods usually fuse modalities before selective scanning, limiting the direct use of auxiliary information in parameter generation. We propose Cross-Modal Selective Scan (CM-S6), which uses lightweight projections to condition selective state-space parameters Δ, B, and C on auxiliary information. These parameters regulate state retention, information writing, and state readout, respectively. With input injection, output calibration, and five tanh-bounded learnable coefficients, CM-S6 forms an input-parameter-output fusion mechanism without increasing backbone width or depth. Across ten independent runs, CM-S6 achieves OA values of 92.11 ± 0.91%, 81.04 ± 1.94%, and 92.77 ± 0.94% on Houston 2013, Augsburg, and MUUFL Gulfport, respectively, using fewer than 1 M parameters, corresponding to 1.9–2.9% of the high-capacity compared baselines. Paired tests detected no significant OA difference from MCAMamba on Houston 2013 or from HLMamba and PICNet on Augsburg, while CM-S6 shows significant OA gains over MSFMamba on Augsburg and MUUFL Gulfport and over DSFormer on MUUFL Gulfport. CM-S6(L) retains parameter-level modulation, reduces model size to approximately 0.19 M parameters, and increases throughput by 3.64–3.94×, with a dataset-dependent accuracy trade-off. CM-S6 offers an alternative for multimodal fusion under resource-constrained conditions.

title: Factors Affecting Farmers' Decision to Sell Premature Onion Gardens as Opposed to Mature-Harvested Bulbs in Ntungamo District
abstract: While Ntungamo District in Uganda is well known for onion production, it is not clear how farmers make the decision to sell premature onion gardens and mature onion bulbs. The study used a cross-sectional design with a convergent parallel approach. A sample size of 140 onion growers were selected through Cochran’s formula using the given confidence level of 95%, and 5 key informant traders were purposively selected. The demographic profile reveals that onion farming in Ntungamo District is predominantly a male-dominated activity (67.9%), with most farmers being married (94.3%) and in their productive working years (median age 40 years). Education levels are relatively low, with 52.1% having only primary education. Many farmers (60.7%) rely solely on onion farming as their primary income source, indicating vulnerability to financial shocks. Access to credit is relatively high at 74.3%, while extension access is limited, with 35.0% receiving no extension visits in the past year. Farmers have a median of 10 years of experience in onion farming, suggesting an established enterprise with accumulated knowledge. The median landholding of 2.0 acres characterises farmers as smallholders. The data was analysed using a binary logistic regression model with a good fit for the model (McFadden R = 0.183), with 72% of the decision rightly predicted. Four determinants influence the marketing decisions of the farmers namely; Distance of farmers to market (OR=1.437; P =0.016), Availability of credit (OR =0.275; P =0.010), Farm type ( primary source of Income) (OR = 0.184;P < 0.001), Area of land( Total acres owned) (OR =1.229; P = 0.027). Farmers located farther away were 43.7% more likely to sell immature gardens for every additional kilometre moved. Farmers with access to credit were 72.5 % less likely to sell immature gardens. Farmers cultivating mixed crops were 81.6% less likely to sell immature gardens in comparison to onion-only farmers. A farmer was more likely to sell immature gardens for every acre of land, with a 23% increase. The demographics of age, sex, education, household members, extension visits, farm experience and association membership were not statistically significant. Farmers' decisions on marketing are economic rather than demographic, and it can be concluded that it is the economic-related factors of marketing which are affecting these decisions, not the demographic factors, because four determinants (market accessibility, credit access, farmer type and plot land owned) were found to affect the marketing of immature gardens. Investment in post-harvest facilities should be made, accessible credit schemes for post-harvest activities should be provided, farmers encouraged to diversify their income sources, and farmer groups and extension services with their component for market analysis should be strengthened to make marketing more profitable.

title: Digital Technologies for Reducing the Carbon Footprint in the Interests of Sustainable Ecological and Economic Development of Agriculture
abstract: In the context of increasing ecological challenges and the necessity for more sustainable development models, global agriculture faces an important mission to provide food to people. The paper is devoted to the analysis of the main digital technologies and their potential in reducing the carbon footprint and ensuring sustainable ecological and economic development of agriculture. An analysis of the current global and Russian greenhouse gas emissions and their innovative solutions in agriculture and nature management was carried out. A review of the up-to-date technologies used in greenhouses and in the farming sector was presented, namely smart greenhouses and smart farming and their components such as the Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and big data. The innovative production system in agriculture is aimed at changing methods and approaches of monitoring, forecasting and decision-making. The described production system in agriculture optimizes agricultural production, increases its efficiency and the usage of resources (water, energy, fertilizers) and thus reduces greenhouse gas emissions in the agri-food chain.
